transcript.text: We replaced our old condenser dryer with a heat pump one about a month ago and honestly it's driving me mad, a normal load of towels takes nearly 3 and a half hours, the old one did it in about 90 minutes. It also feels barely warm for the first half hour when I open the door to check. Surely that's not right? Is it faulty?

It is very likely not faulty. Heat-pump dryers work like a fridge in reverse, recovering heat rather than generating it with a hot element; this means they run cooler and take significantly longer (often 2–3 hours) than old condenser or vented models, so 'barely warm' air for the first half-hour is normal behaviour. However, to rule out simple efficiency issues, please check that the lint filter in the door opening and any second filter at the bottom are completely clean of fluff, and let me know which programme you selected (e.g., Cottons or Synthetics) as some 'eco' modes take even longer.

Ok I clean the fluff filters after every single load, and the other filter at the bottom I cleaned a couple of weeks ago and it looks clean. I've been using Cotton Cupboard Dry with a full load. Does that help?

That suggests it is working as intended. The 'Cotton Cupboard Dry' programme is an eco mode designed to save energy by using lower temperatures and longer times; for a full load of towels on a heat-pump dryer, 3–4 hours is standard. There is no fault here—just a different drying technology compared to your old condenser model.

candidates: Normal heat-pump operation (longer cycle, lower temperature) (high)
Blocked airflow or filters reducing efficiency (medium)
